title: GitHub - Dimoncelli/wiretuple: Zero-dependency Go HTTP reverse proxy that cuts LLM Structured Outputs & Function Calling output tokens by 35-60% via lossless positional tuples
excerpt: Zero-dependency Go HTTP reverse proxy that cuts LLM Structured Outputs & Function Calling output tokens by 35-60% via lossless positional tuples - Dimoncelli/wiretuple
content_html:
Cut 35–60 % of the output tokens of LLM Structured Outputs and Function Calling — losslessly. wiretuple is a single-binary HTTP reverse proxy written in Go with zero external dependencies: your app keeps calling the same API, and repeated JSON keys become positional tuples on the wire.

client ──► wiretuple ──► upstream API
              │
   request:  schema {"items":[{"id","total","currency"}]}
             rewritten to prefixItems + "Tuple: [id, total, currency]"
              │
   response: [["a1", 12.5, "EUR"], ["a2", 3, "USD"]]
             rehydrated to [{"id":"a1","total":12.5,"currency":"EUR"}, ...]
              │
              └─ incremental SSE rehydration, same bytes downstream

Why

A schema that asks for 40 line items with 7 fields makes the model emit the same seven key names 40 times. Those keys are pure overhead: the receiver already knows them from the schema. wiretuple moves the key list into one legend and sends values as positions.

Install

go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o bin/wiretuple ./cmd/wiretuple

No go.mod requirements, no cgo, no runtime data files.

Quickstart

# OpenAI-compatible client
export OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1
./bin/wiretuple -upstream https://api.openai.com

# Anthropic-compatible client
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787
./bin/wiretuple -upstream https://api.anthropic.com

Flags:

Flag Default Meaning
-upstream – upstream base URL (required)
-listen 127.0.0.1:8787 listen address
-break-even 5.0 minimum net savings (%) to rewrite a schema
-legend-tokens 0 fixed legend cost (0 = estimate)
-activate true master switch
-shadow <path> – passive audit into a SQLite file
-max-body 4 MiB request body limit

Protocol coverage

Provider Endpoint Structured output Function calling
OpenAI /v1/chat/completions response_format.json_schema.schema tools[].function.parameters
Anthropic /v1/messages tool schema in input_schema tools[].input_schema

Both stream: false (recomputed Content-Length) and stream: true (SSE, rehydrating only the JSON fragments) are covered. Anything that is not JSON (for example [DONE] or a non-JSON event) is forwarded byte for byte.

Break-even gate

Small payloads are not worth a legend. The gate estimates saved output tokens against the fixed legend cost and keeps the request byte-identical when net savings are below -break-even:

net_savings_% = (tokens_before - tokens_after - legend_tokens) / tokens_before * 100

A single flat object usually stays untouched; a repeated object array with long keys activates.

Passive audit (--shadow)

./bin/wiretuple -upstream https://api.openai.com -shadow audit.db

Traffic passes through untouched. Each request/response pair is simulated and appended to a zero-dependency SQLite 3 file, readable with any SQLite client:

SELECT count(*), avg(net_savings_pct) FROM shadow_records;

The console prints a summary on shutdown: rows, activated, activation_rate, tokens_before, tokens_after, output_savings, net_savings.

Benchmarks

Deterministic scenarios (e-commerce invoice, dev-tool pull request batch, MCP tool definitions) with structural equality asserted after rehydration:

$ make bench
| Scenario | tokens_before | tokens_after | output_savings_% | net_savings_% | p99_overhead_ms | equality |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| E-commerce invoice line items | 2041 | 801 | 60.8% | 59.2% | 0.095 | OK |
| Dev-tool pull request batch | 1602 | 889 | 44.5% | 43.0% | 0.078 | OK |
| MCP tool invocations batch | 1617 | 711 | 56.0% | 53.7% | 0.084 | OK |

Token counts use a deterministic size model (one token per four UTF-8 bytes), so the table is reproducible without an API key. Equality is checked with reflect.DeepEqual on decoded values plus legend key order.

How it works

  • internal/compiler — lossless SchemaNode, deterministic key order (required first, then lexicographic), tuple schemas with prefixItems and items: false (Draft 2020-12, accepted by structured-output APIs that reject additionalItems), nested tuples, and the rehydration tree.
  • internal/gate — break-even estimator with an injectable token model.
  • internal/rehydrator — byte-level state machine; handles UTF-8 split across chunks, escaped quotes/backslashes, brackets and commas inside strings, nested tuples, and degrades to raw output on shape violations without breaking the stream.
  • internal/proxy — reverse proxy, provider detection, SSE codec, bounded bodies, upstream-only forwarding, cancellation.
  • internal/shadow — passive audit plus a pure-Go SQLite 3 writer.

Development

make test    # go test ./...
make race    # go test -race ./...
make bench   # savings table + equality checks
make build   # bin/wiretuple, bin/wiretuple-bench
make vet
